questions.text: Register map: give the offset, width, reset value and access of every register (the design ID at least). Is the ID register the only register?
questions.default: One 32-bit read-only register ID at offset 0x00, reset 0x50494E47, access RO, no other registers
questions.reason: spec.md says the design ID reads PING through the shell but gives no offset, so the map is proposed here and must be confirmed
questions.answer: One 32-bit read-only register ID at offset 0x00, reset 0x50494E47, access RO, no other registers

questions.text: What MAC address should the board use?
questions.reason: spec.md asks for a MAC address without giving a value and the locally administered range avoids clashing with vendor addresses

questions.text: Should the board answer ARP requests for 192.168.1.50?
questions.default: Yes, answer ARP requests for 192.168.1.50 with an ARP reply
questions.reason: other machines must learn the MAC address before they can send echo requests on a LAN, so ping fails without ARP
questions.answer: Yes, answer ARP requests for 192.168.1.50 with an ARP reply

questions.text: Should the LED also light for ARP replies?
questions.default: No, the LED lights only for ICMP echo replies
questions.reason: spec.md says light the LED each time a reply is sent, read as ping replies; ARP is a separate protocol
questions.answer: No, the LED lights only for ICMP echo replies

questions.text: How long should the LED stay lit after a reply?
questions.default: LED_HOLD_CYCLES 10000000, which is 100 ms at 100 MHz
questions.reason: spec.md gives no duration and 100 ms is long enough to see a single reply
questions.answer: LED_HOLD_CYCLES 10000000, which is 100 ms at 100 MHz

questions.text: Should broadcast or multicast echo requests be answered?
questions.default: No, only unicast echo requests addressed to 192.168.1.50 are answered
questions.reason: spec.md names one fixed address and answering broadcasts would reply to every host on the segment
questions.answer: No, only unicast echo requests addressed to 192.168.1.50 are answered

questions.text: Should fragmented IPv4 packets or echo requests with payloads larger than one frame be handled?
questions.default: No, fragmented packets are dropped and echo payloads are limited to what fits in one 1518-byte frame
questions.reason: reassembly is not requested and the frame buffer holds one frame
questions.answer: No, fragmented packets are dropped and echo payloads are limited to what fits in one 1518-byte frame

questions.default: No, the design runs at 100 Mb/s only
questions.reason: the RMII clock enable for 10 Mb/s is not requested and the spec names no link speed
questions.answer: No, the design runs at 100 Mb/s only

questions.text: Which TTL value is used in the reply?
questions.reason: 64 is the common default TTL for IPv4 hosts and spec.md gives no value

questions.text: Should the design check the Ethernet FCS on receive and append it on transmit?
questions.default: Yes, bad-FCS frames are dropped and the FCS is generated on every transmitted frame
questions.reason: without FCS handling the PHY-facing frames are invalid on a real network
questions.answer: Yes, bad-FCS frames are dropped and the FCS is generated on every transmitted frame
